title: Coalescing a parked Codex prompt silently discards a user prompt that is already in the transcript
outcome:
Round-7 review (Claude N1). Not a regression — the old superseded-waiter path dropped it too — but the parking rule makes it a DELIBERATE design point, so it should be a decision, not an accident.

src/codex.rs:904-917: when a second prompt arrives during an in-flight thread setup, it REPLACES the one parked on the setup. The first prompt never reaches Codex. But its Message::Text was already pushed to the session and its turn already 'started' (src/turn_dispatch.rs:362-371).

User-visible result: their message sits in the transcript with no answer, no error, and no retry. The only trace is an eprintln! on stderr.

OPTIONS: (a) fail that turn with a visible error, or (b) re-queue the superseded prompt onto queued_prompts so it runs after the setup completes. (b) is probably right — the user typed it, they meant it.

Related: tm-3nd (parked prompt has no independent timeout / no 'waiting for thread setup' affordance) — same UX surface, different mechanism.
